# Simultaneous internal compensation with both far legs arbitrary

22 October 2026. This removes BOTH far-leg cutoffs from the
[internal pair theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_INTERNAL_LONG_PAIR.md), retaining
incident ten at E and the full-original H3 chain. The proof uses the
[actual-owner coupling](SECONDARY_TEN_INTERNAL_SHORT_PAIR.md), the
[old T frontier](SECONDARY_TEN_LEFT_CHAIN_EXTERIOR.md), and the
[old E frontier](SECONDARY_TEN_E_FAR_FRONTIER.md). The latter is a
new written dependency, not a previously independently accepted theorem.

## Hypotheses and theorem

Retain every endpoint, original support and matching in H3, with even
w_j>=12,z_j>=24, odd a_0, even s_0, even root breadth at least six,

    a_(j+1)=a_j+z_j-6, s_(j+1)=s_j-w_(j+1)-12.

Let J be any subset of the internal indices. At each i in J, choose

    R_i=U(L_i,10,f_i), chart(a_i-11+r,C_i+1-c),
    T_i=U(M_i,4,g_i), chart(a_i-8+r,s_i+1-c),
    C_i=s_i+w_i+13,
    L_i=w_i+M_i+14+q_i,
    M_i>=6, f_i,g_i>=4, q_i>=0, all even.

Assume that every chosen original is endpoint-disjoint from H3 and from
every other chosen original. Their supports remain immutable in the
event definition. No complete extension is required for this selected-
union theorem. In particular it applies to the actual owners at any
selected incident-ten E blocks in a complete even-U/rotor extension:
the coupling and distinctness theorem supplies these hypotheses.

Write

    F_i=s_i-M_i-q_i, G_i=s_i+1-M_i,
    b_i=a_i-11+f_i, y_i=a_i-8+g_i.

Here F_i,b_i are even and G_i,y_i are odd. Let d_i be the old E
deduction in the E-frontier table, and delta_i the old T deduction.
Thus 0<=d_i<=2, delta_i is zero or one, and delta_i=1 forces M_i>=28.
Define epsilon_i=1 exactly when q_i=0 and b_i<y_i; otherwise zero.
Define chi_i=1 exactly when ALL the following hold:

    q_i=0;
    k>i is the first old E-frontier block;
    F_i=s_k-4, b_i=a_k-3, y_i>=a_k-2.

Set chi_i=0 when no such k exists. Then the selected-union increment is
exactly

    DeltaPhi = sum_(i in J)
      (M_i-d_i-delta_i-2epsilon_i+2chi_i) >=4|J|.      (1)

The FULL endpoint tile footprints of distinct pairs are automatically
disjoint, although each of f_i,g_i can be arbitrarily large. No
disjointness of these tile footprints is assumed. It follows from the
width coupling and actual endpoint disjointness, as proved below.

Only NEW increments relative to the single H3 inventory are counted.
The theorem does not allocate the remaining originals' losses or prove
a global 5/6 improvement, arbitrary-grid catalogue exhaustion or the
rectangular-grid triple equality. Deeper E incident legs remain open.

## Exact one-pair ledger

Suppress i. Separately against H3, the two frontier theorems give

    DeltaPhi(R|H3)=1-d,
    DeltaPhi(T|H3)=M-1-delta.                         (2)

All mixed full tiles and directed events here retain their original
physical coordinates and owner labels. Neither receipt uses another
new owner's negative mass or an old-prefix reserve.

R's bar is an entire row of single-owner physical full tiles: its
first row a-11 is even, and its column interval [F,C] has even/odd
ends. Its short near leg is far to the right of T. T's bar/near leg
cannot meet R's far tile column except at T's far edge. Consequently
the ONLY possible mutual endpoint-tile contact is between their far
stems. If q>=2, G>=F+3 puts those stems in distinct physical tile
columns, so there is no mutual event or joint full tile.

For q=0, G=F+1. R occupies [a-11,b] in the left column F, and T
occupies [a-8,y] in the right column F+1. The entry tile at even row
a-9 has only T's lower-right cell. Its horizontal directions target
original supports, so it has no mutual event or new full tile.

Put

    A={r even: a-7<=r<=min(b,y-1)},
    B={r even: a-7<=r<=min(b-2,y-1)}.

For every r in A there are exactly two mutual directed events:

    R:(r,F)->T:(r,F+1), T:(r,F+1)->R:(r,F).

At odd rows both targets are original supports of the respective
owners. The mutual two-owner full tiles have top-left (r,F) for
r in B. These physical tiles belong to neither separate old receipt.
Because b is even, y is odd, and f,g>=4,

    |A|-|B| = [b<y] = epsilon.

Thus their mutual two-owner signed contribution is -2epsilon for
arbitrary f and g, independently of the number of shared full tiles.

There is one possible additional mixed full tile involving H3,R,T.
R and T must each have an endpoint there, so q=0 and the tile is in
their shared far column. Every interior tile with two R endpoints and
two T endpoints is already in B. The entry tile lacks its upper-right
endpoint in H3 as well: F+1<=s_i-5 separates it from the own and
earlier old blocks, and every later block starts below the entry.
After T's far terminal, its last tile already contains both right
endpoints; no half-terminal in the opposite parity creates another case.

The only remaining possibility is R's terminal tile with upper-left R,
both right cells T, and lower-left old. In the E frontier table:

- At F=s_k-4, the first old left endpoint is X_k at row a_k-2.
  This makes the tile full exactly when b=a_k-3 and y>=a_k-2.
  Its top-left is (a_k-3,F). It is not full in either separate old
  receipt, since that receipt lacks respectively the two T cells or
  the R cell. This is precisely chi=1.
- At F=s_k-2, a lower-left Z endpoint can first occur when b=a_k-3.
  But T's same first frontier has G=s_k-1 and requires y<=a_k-6.
  T cannot occupy the right cells in this terminal tile.
- At F=s_k, R's legal bound b<=a_k-5 stops above the first same-
  column old Z endpoint at a_k-3. There is no lower-left old endpoint.
- At F>=s_k+2, the first old left endpoint is P's bar at a_k-8.
  Its terminal candidate b=a_k-9 again has T bound y<=a_k-10,
  excluding right-cell occupation. Without a frontier there are no
  old endpoints in the shared tile column.

The first frontiers of R and T are the SAME k in these q=0 cases:
F>=s_k-4 iff G>=s_k-3. The additional triple-owner tile contributes
2chi. Events remain pairwise directed endpoint adjacencies; a third
owner cannot create a further event beyond the separate and mutual
event sets. Adding (2), the mutual receipt and this tile proves the
exact one-pair expression in (1).

## Why the two deductions cannot stack

We prove the decisive inequality

    d+2epsilon<=2.                                   (3)

If q>=2 then epsilon=0 and d<=2. If q=0 and d=0 the conclusion is
immediate. For q=0 and d>0, the legal R/T frontiers are coupled:

| F | R deduction active only at | T must satisfy |
|---|---|---|
| s_k-2 | d=1, b=a_k-3 | y<=a_k-6 |
| s_k | d=2, b=a_k-7 or a_k-5 | y<=a_k-10 |
| F>=s_k+2 | d=1, b=a_k-9 | y<=a_k-10 |

In EVERY row y<b, so epsilon=0. The X column has no R deduction.
This proves (3) in all cases without a dimension cutoff.

Since chi>=0, one pair's exact increment is at least M-2-delta.
For delta=0 use M>=6 to obtain at least four. For delta=1 the T
frontier identity gives M=s_i-s_k+4>=28, so the increment is at
least25. The exceptional old T debit is paid once from its OWN M-1
mass; it is neither ignored nor charged to a different pair.

The +2chi term is necessary for the exact identity. For example, use
three uniform blocks a_0=31,s_0=0,w_j=12,z_j=24 and i=1. Choose

    M=28,q=0,f=26,g=24, L=54.

Then F=-52=s_2-4,b=64=a_2-3,y=65=a_2-2. Here
d=0,delta=1,epsilon=1,chi=1, so the exact pair increment is27,
rather than25. The triple-owner full tile has top-left (64,-52).
This is an endpoint-disjoint partial witness, not a complete-extension
existence claim.

## Automatic separation of arbitrary selected pairs

The width relation gives

    F_j=G_j-1-q_j<=G_j-1, s_j+1<C_j.

Thus EVERY endpoint tile column of pair j, including the whole T_j,
is within the tile-column interval of the aligned R_j bar [F_j,C_j].
All its endpoint rows are at least a_j-11. This bar is the crucial
additional guard when both far legs are unbounded.

Take i<j. The R_i bar/near leg and T_i bar/near leg all end at row
at most a_i-1. Since a_j>=a_i+18, their endpoint tiles lie strictly
above the first even R_j bar row a_j-11>=a_i+7. Only either of
pair i's two long far columns can reach pair j's endpoint tiles.

Consider either such continuous far stem, at column x and terminal t.
Its start is above a_j-11. If its physical tile column meets pair j's
footprint, it also meets the R_j bar's tile-column interval. Because
the bar's left end is even and right end odd, this implies

    F_j<=x<=C_j.

If t>=a_j-11, the stem contains the actual R_j bar endpoint
(a_j-11,x), contrary to the assumed endpoint disjointness of these
originals. Therefore t<a_j-11. The first bar row is even, so this
strict bound also separates their PHYSICAL tile rows, whether t is
even (R_i) or odd (T_i). Otherwise their tile columns were separated
already. This argument handles both far stems and all later endpoints,
including T_j, with no imposed far-length bound.

Every two selected pairs therefore have disjoint FULL endpoint tile
footprints. The argument does not require ordering by widths, nesting
of the far columns, support closure, or a separately postulated allocation.

## Exact simultaneous accounting and verification scope

Every newly full mixed tile and every new intratile directed event
contains a new endpoint, so lies in its pair's endpoint tile footprint.
No two pairs can share such a physical tile or event. Each new original's
immutable charge contributes once. New receipts are therefore the
disjoint union of the one-pair receipts, and the exact identity and
lower bound (1) follow. Shared old owners do not re-credit their mass
or duplicate their old events. Only changes relative to H3 are added.

The companion verifier compares the complete predicted physical full-tile
and owner-labelled event SETS, including the triple-owner correction,
then checks automatic pair-footprint separation and exact simultaneous
addition for endpoint-disjoint selected batches. The scoped Lean module
checks parity/column gates, aligned-bar separation, nonstacking and the
conditional scalar/list ledger. General source-chart exhaustion and actual-
owner normalization remain written mathematical arguments.

Validation passed 11,568 exact one-pair full/event SET comparisons,
including 12 activated triple-owner corrections and all frontier phases;
60 endpoint-disjoint batches of four or five pairs; and two/five/eleven-
pair groups with both far legs around 2000 and exact gains 2326,6816,19230.
The explicit triple-owner witness has gain27 and the old-loss sharp
witness gain4. Local standalone Lean passed29declarations/21theorems
with individual ordinary-axiom reports and no warnings/sorry/native axioms
in the final run. See the
[validation record](../output/secondary-ten-both-far-compensation-validation.json).

The previously accepted short-pair audit and active arbitrary-t-far
audit do not cover this new theorem or its new E-frontier dependency.
No independent ACCEPT is claimed without a separate completed review.
The submitted 11 October manuscript and primary star-forming results
are preserved; full-family allocation and the global grid targets remain
open.

# Exact old-chain frontier for arbitrary internal E far legs

22 October 2026. Retain every original endpoint, support and matching of
the full H3 chain defined in
[the left-chain exterior theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_LEFT_CHAIN_EXTERIOR.md).
The even dimensions satisfy w_j>=12,z_j>=24, the anchors a_j are odd,
the offsets s_j are even, and

    a_(j+1)=a_j+z_j-6, s_(j+1)=s_j-w_(j+1)-12.

This note removes the E far-leg cutoff for ONE original against H3.
It does not yet add arbitrary other new owners. The proposed arbitrary-
both-far simultaneous compensation theorem remains open.

## Statement

Fix an internal index i>=1 and a full original

    R=U(L,10,f), chart(r,c)=(a_i-11+r,C_i+1-c),
    C_i=s_i+w_i+13, L>=w_i+20, f>=4, L,f even.

The width condition is necessary whenever R is an actual E owner with
incident ten: the actual-owner coupling gives L>=w_i+M+14 with M>=6.
For the present theorem, completeness is unnecessary; R need only be
endpoint-disjoint from H3. Its even far column and terminal row are

    F=C_i+1-L<=s_i-6, b=a_i-11+f.

Let k>i be the first index with F>=s_k-4, if it exists. The following
table is exact. The deduction d is defined only on the legal rows.

| Far column | Endpoint-disjoint iff | Deduction d |
|---|---|---|
| No k | Every even f>=4 | 0 |
| F=s_k-4 | b<=a_k-3 | 0 |
| F=s_k-2 | b<=a_k-3 | 1 if b=a_k-3, otherwise 0 |
| F=s_k | b<=a_k-5 | 2 if b is a_k-7 or a_k-5, otherwise 0 |
| s_k+2<=F<=s_(k-1)-6 | b<=a_k-9 | 1 if b=a_k-9, otherwise 0 |

For every legal R,

    Phi(H3 union {R})-Phi(H3)=1-d>=-1.                 (1)

The minimum -1 occurs exactly in the third finite-contact row with
b in {a_k-7,a_k-5}. It is attained by endpoint-disjoint originals.
These witnesses need not admit a complete extension. A negative R
marginal neither refutes a joint-pair compensation rule nor the global
target inequality.

## First-contact proof

Every old block, including its P,Z,X originals, has minimum endpoint
column s_j-4. The far strip of R uses the physical tile column {F,F+1}.
For j<=i, F<=s_i-6 puts that tile strictly to the left of every old
endpoint. If k exists, minimality and even parity give

    s_k-4<=F<=s_(k-1)-6.

Every block before k is separated by the same tile-column argument.
The R bar is above its own P bar and above all later blocks; earlier
blocks are to its right. Its fixed near leg has the same four-full-
tile/eight-event receipt as in the short-pair theorem. Extending its
far leg therefore changes only the strip at {F,F+1}.

Substitution in the full original charts of block k gives the first
same-column endpoint and the relevant partner-column profile:

| F | First old endpoint in column F | Relevant endpoints at F+1 |
|---|---|---|
| s_k-4 | X_k at row a_k-2 | None before the legal terminal tile |
| s_k-2 | Z_k at row a_k-2 | Z_k starts at row a_k-4 |
| s_k | Z_k at row a_k-3 | P_k far stem at rows a_k-8,...,a_k-4 |
| F>=s_k+2 | P_k bar at row a_k-8 | None above that bar |

R occupies every far-column row from a_i-11 through b. Its start is
above each displayed first endpoint. Avoiding that endpoint, with b
even, gives exactly the legal bounds in the statement. In particular
the last case is blocked by the P BAR, even when another old stem
continues farther down. Treating that stem as the first obstacle would
give an incorrect legal depth.

These bounds are sufficient as well. R's bar and near leg have already
been separated; earlier blocks cannot meet the far tile column. All
legal terminals satisfy b<=a_k-3. Every block after k starts at row at
least a_(k+1)-8>=a_k+10, below this terminal and its physical tile.
There is no later block when k is last. If k does not exist, column
separation excludes every old endpoint and intratile receipt for any f.
This proves the exact collision table without a depth or chain cutoff.

## Exact physical receipts

All coordinates below are absolute. A physical tile is specified by
its even top-left coordinate; rows increase downward. Old supports stay
excluded from directed events even if another owner consumes them.

The near receipt has four new mixed full tiles and eight new directed
events, hence signed value zero. R has charge -1 and adds negative
mass one. The far receipt is disjoint from these near tiles.

At F=s_k-4, even the last legal terminal b=a_k-3 creates no event:
R's downward target is its original axial support, and X_k's upward
target is X_k's original axial support. There is no mixed full tile.

At F=s_k-2, only b=a_k-3 activates a receipt. The tile with top-left
(a_k-3,F) has R at its upper-left cell and Z_k at the other three.
The two horizontal directions at row b and the upward Z_k direction
from (b+1,F) survive. R's downward direction is excluded by its axial
support. Thus there is one new mixed full tile and three new events,
with signed value -1. Earlier even terminals create no receipt.

At F=s_k, activation occurs at b=a_k-7 or a_k-5. Write

    b=a_k-7+2h, h in {0,1}.

The new mixed full tiles have top-left (a_k-7,F) when h=1 and none
when h=0. For each t=0,...,h the events are exactly

    R:(a_k-7+2t,F) -> P_k:(a_k-7+2t,F+1),
    P_k:(a_k-7+2t,F+1) -> R:(a_k-7+2t,F).

At odd rows the horizontal directions target original supports of the
respective originals. The entry tile, where P_k first occupies its
lower-right cell, has no event or full tile. The terminal tile has the
two displayed events and lacks R's lower-left cell. Therefore the far
receipt has h new mixed full tiles and 2h+2 events, signed value -2.
All earlier terminals have zero far receipt. Z_k in the same column
prevents any continuation to X_k or another later profile.

In the remaining column range only b=a_k-9 activates a receipt. There
is a single upward event P_k:(b+1,F)->R:(b,F); R's reverse direction
targets its original axial support. The partner cells are absent, so
there is no new full tile. The signed value is -1.

These profiles exhaust the legal far strip. Adding its signed value
to the near value zero and mass one proves (1). Every mixed full tile
and owner-labelled event is counted as a physical set element once.
No old-prefix reserve or other new owner's negative mass is used.

## A sharp local witness and the remaining simultaneous problem

Take a_0=31,s_0=0, three blocks with all w_j=12,z_j=24 and root
breadth six. At i=1, a_i=49,s_i=-24,C_i=1. Let

    R=U(50,10,22), chart(r,c)=(38+r,2-c).

Then F=-48=s_2 and b=60=a_2-7. R is endpoint-disjoint from H3 and
has exact increment -1. Its actual forced t partner, if it exists,
has left incident four and width at most 24 by the coupling inequality.
The witness alone is not a complete configuration or a counterexample
to simultaneous pair gain >=4m.

The frontier theorem proves that a long R can lose at most two units
to the OLD chain. Extending it to H3 plus all selected new T owners
requires showing that their terminal losses cannot stack on that same
R terminal. A discovery run checked 18,111 such marginals with minimum
-1, but this is evidence for that extension, not its proof. The
simultaneous arbitrary-both-far inequality is not asserted here.

The companion verifier checks exact collision decisions and complete
mixed-full-tile and owner-labelled-event SETS at every frontier phase,
translated and nonuniform chains, and large far depths. The standalone
Lean module checks the frontier parity arithmetic, conditional receipt
identity and sharp lower bound. Full original geometric exhaustion is
the written proof above; it is not claimed to be fully formalized.

Validation passed 19,712 collision decisions and 10,482 exact full/event
set comparisons, with all four frontier phases and far depths up to 2000.
Local standalone Lean passed 18 declarations, including 17 theorems;
individual axiom reports contain only ordinary axioms, with no warnings,
sorry or native axioms. No independent review of this new frontier theorem
has been submitted or accepted. The earlier arbitrary-t-far audit continues
under its own original task; it does not review this new note.
See the [validation record](../output/secondary-ten-e-far-frontier-validation.json).

The global 5/6 improvement, full-family allocation and rectangular-grid
triple equality remain open. The submitted 11 October manuscript stays
unchanged.

# Internal short E owners force a paired consumer and admit simultaneous compensation

22 October 2026. Retain all H3 original endpoint/support/matching records,
the recurrence, and the explicit complete full-even-U/rotor model from
[the internal E barrier](SECONDARY_TEN_INTERNAL_E_BARRIER.md). In particular,
actual owners of all t_j=(a_j-4,s_j) and y_j=(a_j-1,C_j), C_j=s_j+w_j+13,
are distinct north-terminal full U originals. The internal y owner R_j
is left with incident depth d>=10. No arbitrary-grid catalogue exhaustion
or complete-extension existence is asserted.

## Actual-owner coupling at incident depth ten

Fix any internal j and write a=a_j,s=s_j,w=w_j,C=s+w+13.
Suppose its actual E owner has incident depth ten:

    R=U(L,10,f), chart(r,c)->(a-11+r,C+1-c), f>=4 even.

Then its actual t owner T necessarily has the form

    T=U(M,4,g), chart(r,c)->(a-8+r,s+1-c),
    M,g even, M>=6,g>=4, and L>=w+M+14.                 (1)

This classifies T's orientation and incident leg, and bounds its breadth;
it does not classify g or assert sufficiency. In particular L>=w+20.
The former tight R breadth w+14 is impossible at incident ten for EVERY
far depth, not merely the sampled negative-marginal example.

Proof. Put F=C+1-L, the R far column. R occupies all far-column rows
a-11,...,a-11+f, including a-8. P_j's bar row a-8 occupies every column
s+1,...,C-1. Since L>=6, F<=C-5, so endpoint disjointness forces F<=s,
equivalently L>=w+14. Every R bar point at row a-10 and columns F,...,C
is an endpoint, including (a-10,s).

The actual t owner has an incident column at s ending at row a-4. If
its even incident depth were at least six, that column would include
(a-10,s), colliding with R. Hence its depth is four. A right depth-four
t owner has bar endpoint (a-8,s+1), colliding with P. It must be left,
in the displayed chart. Its bar row a-8 occupies columns G=s-M+1,...,s.
R contains (a-8,F); since F<=s, avoiding T requires F<G, hence F<=s-M.
Substitution yields L>=w+M+14. All comparisons concern complete original
endpoint sets, including bar rows zero and one. The old same-color
terminal argument ensures R and T are distinct actual originals.

## A further restriction on the first remaining internal deep B branch

If j+1<n and a right actual t_(j+1) owner has breadth w+w_(j+1)+26
and incident D=z_j+6, the earlier internal depth gap forces its far
depth to equal four. Call this owner B. Its far column C occupies
[a-16,a-12]. Any E owner with d>=12 would contain (a-12,C), so the
actual R has d=10 and (1) applies.

Put v=w_(j+1) and s'=s-v-12. B's near column s' contains row a-10
because its incident interval is [a-16,a+z_j-10], with z_j>=24.
R's lower bar occupies [F,C] at that row. Thus F>s'. Both columns
are even, so F>=s'+2, and

    w+M+14 <= L <= w+v+24, hence M<=v+10.              (2)

This is a necessary finite WIDTH window inside an unbounded geometric
family; no full extension or sufficiency of (2) is asserted. The branch
is not eliminated merely because the previous D=z+4 branch was.

## Exact compensation when both far legs are four

Assume in addition f=g=4 for these actual R and T. Write

    L=w+M+14+q, q>=0 even, F=s-M-q, G=s-M+1.

For EVERY allowed H3 chain and internal j, the two displayed full
originals are endpoint-disjoint from ALL H3 and from each other. Their
selected-union increment relative to H3 is exactly

    DeltaPhi({R,T}|H3)=M-2*[q=0] >=4.                  (3)

Here Phi=N+S+2F_full-E_foreign, with immutable original source charges,
mixed full physical tiles and owner-labelled directed intratile events
excluding targets in the source's ORIGINAL support set. No arbitrary
exterior-owner monotonicity is used.

First verify geometric separation from ALL originals. R occupies rows
a-11,...,a-1, and T rows a-8,...,a-4. R's far column F<=s-6 lies
strictly left of every endpoint of block j and its west rotor/small U,
whose minimum column is s-4. T's far column G<=s-5 is also outside
their endpoints. At the limiting G=s-5, adjacency to old column s-4
crosses a physical tile-column boundary, so there is no intratile event.
R's far tip ends at a-7, above every current west-rotor endpoint (rows>=a-4).
R and T bars lie above the original body, apart from T's near contact
with P; R's near column stops at y, immediately above old E at (a,C).

At all columns <=C, every earlier-block endpoint is at row at most a-16:
the nearest predecessor's small U ends at a-z_(j-1)+8<=a-16; its other
left-side body endpoints are higher. The predecessor's long V column
is C+1, across the physical tile boundary from odd C; the remaining
earlier long columns are farther right. Every later-block body starts
at least a_(j+1)-8>=a+10, and later long columns start still lower.
Thus no earlier/later original adds a same-tile receipt to R or T.
This accounts for the whole retained chain, not just P_j.

Each original's immutable charge is used ONCE. R has charge -1; T has
